method: Claude Browser tools, own tab (tab-3). Pages are client-rendered; the browser address bar collapses to https://nexon.com after navigation, so URLs below are the canonical addresses typed into navigate and confirmed via location.href in-page. Text captured with get_page_text and with document.body.innerText slices via javascript_tool. The link-skills page renders its data in 35 <table> elements; get_page_text preserved every cell as tab-separated text, and the capture was verified complete against document.body.innerText.length (31749 chars).

pages.staleness: SELF-DECLARED STALE. Verbatim banner at top of page: "[Note] This guide is out of date as of the v.269 update, which revamped the V Matrix system. It will be updated soon."

promptInjectionCheck.detail: None of the three pages contained text addressed to an agent or instructing any action. The only imperative text is ordinary reader guidance, e.g. "You can directly move to the information you want by searching it with [Ctrl + F]." Nothing was acted on.

unlockAndUpgradeLadder.quote: All Jobs possess Link Skills, skills that can be shared with your other characters in the same world to give them a power boost. The skills' effects are always applied to the character themselves and, once you reach Lv. 70, you can choose another one of your characters within the same world to transfer the corresponding skill.
unlockAndUpgradeLadder.quote2: When your linked character reaches Lv. 120, the effects get upgraded and you can receive the effects of Lv. 2, and at Lv. 210, the effects are upgraded again and you receive the effects of Lv. 3.
unlockAndUpgradeLadder.quote3: Lv. 1 can be reached at Lv. 70, Lv. 2 can be reached at Lv. 120, and Lv. 3 can be reached at Lv. 210.
unlockAndUpgradeLadder.note: quote3 is repeated verbatim under every non-stacking job section on the page.

transferCap.quote: List of all of the Link Skills currently transferred to the current character (you can transfer up to 12 at a time).

transferFrequency.quote: Link Skills can be transferred an unlimited number of times per day.

transferPrerequisite.quote: All Jobs (excluding Zero) need to reach their 1st Job Advancement in order to transfer their Link Skills.

selfBenefit.quote: A character always benefits from their own Link Skills, even if has been transferred to another character.

teachingQuest.quote: Once your character reaches Lv. 70, you can learn how to share your link skills with the "Teaching Link Skills" quest via the quest notifier.
teachingQuest.quote2: You can transfer Link Skills once you reach Lv. 70, even if you don't finish the quest.

manager.quote: Link Skill Transfers can be managed via the "Link Manager" skill on your Beginner Skill tab.

stackingRules.cygnusAndResistance: Cygnus Knights' and Resistance's Link Skills can be stacked. For example, if you level-up two Cygnus Knights characters to Lv. 120, the Link Skill becomes Lv. 4.
stackingRules.explorer: If you have different characters with the same Explorer job in the same world, their Link Skills can be stacked up to three times to the same character.
stackingRules.explorerExample: For example, three Explorer Warrior characters could transfer each of their Link Skills to the same character on that world, and they would stack.
stackingRules.zeroTip: Zero characters can upgrade their Link Skills to Lv. 5 by completing Chapter 8 of their storyline.
stackingRules.internalContradiction: The page's own TIPS block says Zero reaches Lv. 5 by completing "Chapter 8", while the Zero section says "Link Skills level up for Zero characters as they complete Acts 2 - 4, and completing Act 8 will upgrade the Link Skill to Lv. 6." Lv. 5 vs Lv. 6, Chapter vs Act. NEXON contradicts itself here; do not treat either number as settled.

unlockLevel.quote: Once you reach Lv. 200 and complete job advancement quests, you can begin to utilize 5th Job skills.

skillTypes.quote: Shared Skills: Skills that can be used by any character, regardless of Class or Job.
skillTypes.quote2: Class-Specific Skills: Skills that can be used by a specific Class (Warrior, Magician, Bowman, Thief, and Pirate).
skillTypes.quote3: Job Skills: Skills that can only be used by that Job, similar to 1st through 4th Job Skills.

howObtained.quote: 5th Job Skills are obtained, and have their Skill Levels boosted, by equipping Nodes on the V Matrix. These Nodes can be chosen, combined, and enhanced by players through the V Matrix, and you can learn more about it in the V Matrix Maple Guide.

masterLevel.note: Every 5th Job skill listed on the page, shared and job alike, is tagged '[Master Level: 25]'. 459 occurrences of the string 'Master Level' in the page text, and no other master-level value appears.

Completion of all Esfera story quests

fifthJob.bowMasterNote: "Quiver Cartridge" is NOT among Bow Master's 5th Job skills on this guide; the closest name is "Quiver Barrage". The owner's 6th Job node is "Quiver Cartridge/Phoenix Mastery Enhancement", so Quiver Cartridge is a pre-5th-job skill that a boost node / HEXA Mastery core targets, not a 5th Job node skill. The repo's bow-master.json already places Quiver Cartridge + Phoenix as boost-node group 3, which is consistent with this.
fifthJob.erelLightAndSiaAstellePresence: Both Erel Light and Sia Astelle DO appear in this page's job-category table (Erel Light under Warrior/Other, Sia Astelle under Magician/Other), which is why their absence from the link-skills page is notable rather than explicable by 'the guide site does not know these classes yet'.

vMatrix.stalenessBanner: [Note] This guide is out of date as of the v.269 update, which revamped the V Matrix system. It will be updated soon.

unlock.quote: Characters who have advanced to their 5th Job Advancement will be able to utilize the V Matrix system, allowing them to equip Nodes on their V Matrix to obtain new skills or enhance specific skills, and even raise the power of those skills through Node enhancements!

nodeTypes.skillNodes: Skill Nodes: Nodes to obtain 5th Job Skills.
nodeTypes.boostNodes: Boost Nodes: Nodes that can be used to enhance a character's 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Job Skills, as well as Hyper Skills.
nodeTypes.specialNodes: Special Nodes: Once the requirements are met, special effects are activated with these Nodes.

boostNodeComposition.quote: Boost Nodes consist of 1 main skill and 2 sub-skills. A total of 3 skills make up a single Boost Node.

boostNodePairingRules.quote: When enhancing Nodes, only the same type of Nodes with the same main skill can be enhanced.
boostNodePairingRules.quote2: Also, Boost Nodes with the same main skills cannot be stacked.
boostNodePairingRules.quote3: The skill selected while crafting Nodes becomes the main skill, and sub-skills are assigned randomly.

specialNodeSlotRule.quote: Special Nodes can only be equipped on 1 slot within the V Matrix.

rankCaps.skillNode: A Skill Node's highest Rank is normally 25, but can be increased to up to 30 via Slot Enhancement.
rankCaps.boostNode: A Boost Node's highest Rank is normally 50, but can be increased to up to 55 via Slot Enhancement.

slotEnhancement.pointSource: Every level above Lv. 200 will award you with a Matrix Point that can be used to enhance your Node Slots, increasing the skill level of a Skill or Boost Node equipped in that slot.
slotEnhancement.cap: Each slot can be upgraded up to 5 times. Simply click on a Node Slot, whether filled or empty, and confirm to enhance a slot. Each enhancement costs 1 Matrix Point.
slotEnhancement.noFailure: Enhancing a Node Slot has no chance of failure, and requires no cost beyond the Matrix Points earned from leveling up.
slotEnhancement.reset: This costs 1,000,000 mesos, will reset the enhancement level of all slots, and will refund all spent Matrix Points as well. There is no increase in costs or cooldown on resetting.
slotEnhancement.arithmetic: The Rank of a Skill Node and the level of the Node slot determine the level of the obtained skill (excluding Special Nodes).
slotEnhancement.arithmeticExample: Ex: If a Rank 2 Skill Node is equipped in a Lv. 3 Node slot, then the subsequent Skill will be Lv. 5.
slotEnhancement.specialNodeExclusion: While Special Nodes can be equipped into Enhanced Slots, they will gain no benefit from doing so.

nodestones.quote: Nodestone: You can use this item to obtain Nodes. Nodestones can be earned through events, or through field hunting and content within the Arcane River and Grandis regions.
nodestones.startingRank: Nodes that are initially obtained from Nodestones are Rank 1 and have 0 EXP.
nodestones.experienceNodestones: You can also consume Experience Nodestones to enhance any Node, but cannot be extracted into Node Shards. Experience Nodestones can be acquired through a variety of means, most notably through Events.

enhancementRules.exp: EXP is gained by consuming a Node of the same type as the target Node to enhance it. Once the enhanced Node reaches 100% EXP, you can upgrade it to the next Rank.
enhancementRules.whatCanBeEnhanced: You can only enhance Skill Nodes and Boost Nodes. You cannot enhance Special Nodes.
enhancementRules.ingredientRank: The higher the Rank of a Node used as an ingredient, the more EXP your Node will obtain.
enhancementRules.nodecrafting: You can disassemble Nodes of your choice via Nodecrafting, creating Node Shards which can then be used to craft new Nodes and Nodestones.

vMatrix.terminologyNote: The guide calls the level-up currency 'Matrix Point'. The owner's in-game UI calls them 'V Points' (26 unspent). Either the v.269 revamp renamed them, or the guide's term is simply older. Flag as a naming divergence, not a numeric conflict.

newFacts.fact: A character can have at most 12 link skills transferred to it at one time.
newFacts.quote: List of all of the Link Skills currently transferred to the current character (you can transfer up to 12 at a time).
newFacts.whyItMatters: This is a hard cap the planner does not model. With 53 classes on the roster there are far more than 12 link skills available, so 'level this character for the account' advice is only true if the resulting link would actually make the top 12. A roster recommendation engine that ignores the cap will recommend levelling a character whose link the owner cannot equip.

newFacts.fact: Link skill transfers are free and unlimited per day.
newFacts.quote: Link Skills can be transferred an unlimited number of times per day.
newFacts.whyItMatters: Softens the 12-slot cap: the owner can swap the loadout per activity (bossing vs training) at no cost. The planner can recommend two loadouts rather than one compromise loadout.

newFacts.fact: A character must reach 1st Job Advancement before its link skill can be transferred (Zero excepted).
newFacts.quote: All Jobs (excluding Zero) need to reach their 1st Job Advancement in order to transfer their Link Skills.
newFacts.whyItMatters: A second gate below Lv. 70 that lib/legion.ts does not model.

newFacts.fact: A character always keeps its own link skill even after transferring it away.
newFacts.quote: A character always benefits from their own Link Skills, even if has been transferred to another character.
newFacts.whyItMatters: Means transferring costs the source character nothing - relevant to any UI that implies a trade-off.

newFacts.fact: Explorer link skills stack up to 3 times, once per unique Explorer job in that class branch on the world.
newFacts.quote: If you have different characters with the same Explorer job in the same world, their Link Skills can be stacked up to three times to the same character.
newFacts.whyItMatters: lib/legion.ts's linkLevel() returns 0-3 per character and has no concept of a stacked account-level total. For the owner specifically: Bow Master is an Explorer Bowman, so Marksman and Pathfinder at 210 each add a further 3 levels to Adventurer's Curiosity, taking Critical Rate from +6% to +15%. That is a concrete, quantified 'level these two characters' recommendation the app cannot currently make.

newFacts.fact: Cygnus Blessing reaches Lv. 15 with five Knights at Lv. 210; Spirit of Freedom reaches Lv. 12 with four Resistance characters at Lv. 210; two Knights at Lv. 120 already gives Lv. 4.
newFacts.quote: Cygnus Knights' Link Skills can be stacked, and by leveling up 5 different Knights (Dawn Warrior, Blaze Wizard, Wind Archer, Night Walker, and Thunder Breaker) to Lv. 210, the Link Skill can reach Lv. 15.
newFacts.whyItMatters: Gives the exact account-level payoff curve for the two biggest multi-character link investments. lib/legion.ts caps link level at 3 and so cannot express 'your fourth Cygnus Knight is worth +2 ATT to every character'.

newFacts.fact: Cygnus Blessing pays a bonus to Cygnus Knights themselves starting at Lv. 11: +31 ATT instead of +27, rising to +55 instead of +35 at Lv. 15.
newFacts.quote: Attack Power and Magic ATT: +35 (Cygnus Knights only: +55)
newFacts.whyItMatters: Not modelled anywhere. It means a Cygnus main gets a materially larger return from the same roster investment than a Bow Master main does.

newFacts.fact: Many links carry an own-class-only Damage bonus that the linked character never receives: Phantom, Mercedes, Shade, Evan, Aran +5%; Hoyoung, Luminous +4%; Ren, Zero +5%; Khali +10% vs +7%; Lara +10% vs +7%; Mihile +3%; Explorer Bowman/Pirate/Warrior +6% at Lv. 9.
newFacts.whyItMatters: data/classes.json records only the transferred value for most of these. Any 'what does this link give me' display is correct, but any 'what does this character gain from its own link' display would be understated.

newFacts.fact: Zero's link is levelled by storyline progress, not character level, and the guide contradicts itself on the endpoint: the TIPS block says Lv. 5 via Chapter 8, the Zero section says Lv. 6 via Act 8.
newFacts.quote: Zero characters can upgrade their Link Skills to Lv. 5 by completing Chapter 8 of their storyline.
newFacts.quote2: Link Skills level up for Zero characters as they complete Acts 2 - 4, and completing Act 8 will upgrade the Link Skill to Lv. 6.
newFacts.whyItMatters: lib/legion.ts's nextLink() would tell a Zero owner to grind to 210. That advice is wrong for Zero - the ladder is storyline-gated. data/classes.json already notes this; lib/legion.ts does not, and legion.ts is the file that generates the recommendations.

newFacts.fact: Zero's level ladder is not linear: Lv. 5 is 15% damage reduction / 10% DEF ignore, and Lv. 6 jumps to 20% / 15%.
newFacts.quote:
Reduces your damage receipt by 20%
When attacking, ignore the target's DEF by 15%
newFacts.whyItMatters: Explains the repo's wrong 18%/12% figure - it is what you get by extrapolating the Lv. 1-5 slope one more step. Any other repo value derived by extrapolating a link ladder is now suspect.

newFacts.fact: Explorer Warrior's Invincible Belief cooldown falls with level, 410 sec at Lv. 1 down to 150 sec at Lv. 9.
newFacts.whyItMatters: The repo stores a single cooldown with no level dimension, and the value it stores (90s) is not on the ladder at all.

newFacts.fact: Every 5th Job skill in GMS has Master Level 25.
newFacts.whyItMatters: Uniform across all 459 skill entries on the page. Pairs with the V Matrix rule that a Skill Node's rank normally caps at 25 and reaches 30 via slot enhancement - i.e. the slot enhancement is what takes a 5th job skill past its printed master level.

newFacts.fact: Two shared 5th Job skills are story-gated: Solar Crest requires all Cernium story quests, True Arachnid Reflection requires all Esfera story quests.
newFacts.quote: Completion of all Cernium story quests
newFacts.whyItMatters: These are progression gates the planner could surface as prerequisites. At Lv. 245 the owner has almost certainly cleared both, but any advice given to a lower-level mule needs them.

newFacts.fact: Matrix Points come from levels above 200, one per level; each slot accepts up to 5 enhancements at 1 point each; a full reset costs exactly 1,000,000 mesos and refunds every point, with no cooldown and no escalating cost.
newFacts.quote: Every level above Lv. 200 will award you with a Matrix Point that can be used to enhance your Node Slots, increasing the skill level of a Skill or Boost Node equipped in that slot.
newFacts.quote2: This costs 1,000,000 mesos, will reset the enhancement level of all slots, and will refund all spent Matrix Points as well. There is no increase in costs or cooldown on resetting.
newFacts.whyItMatters: Directly usable for the owner: at Lv. 245 the levels-above-200 count is 45, and 26 are unspent, implying 19 spent. A 1,000,000 meso reset is free in practice at 764% meso obtained, so the planner can safely recommend experimenting with slot allocation. Caveat: the page is self-declared stale as of v.269, and the owner's UI calls these 'V Points', not 'Matrix Points'.

newFacts.fact: Node slot level and node rank add: a Rank 2 skill node in a Lv. 3 slot yields a Lv. 5 skill.
newFacts.quote: Ex: If a Rank 2 Skill Node is equipped in a Lv. 3 Node slot, then the subsequent Skill will be Lv. 5.
newFacts.whyItMatters: The arithmetic is additive, not multiplicative. Lets the planner compute achievable skill levels from a node inventory plus a point budget.

newFacts.fact: Special Nodes occupy exactly one slot, cannot be enhanced, and gain nothing from an enhanced slot.
newFacts.quote: Special Nodes can only be equipped on 1 slot within the V Matrix.
newFacts.quote2: While Special Nodes can be equipped into Enhanced Slots, they will gain no benefit from doing so.
newFacts.whyItMatters: A direct, actionable misplay warning: never spend Matrix Points on the slot holding a special node. The owner's matrix shows 1 special node, so this applies today.

newFacts.fact: Nodestones drop from field hunting and content in the Arcane River and Grandis regions, and from events; Experience Nodestones enhance any node but cannot be disassembled into shards.
newFacts.quote: Nodestones can be earned through events, or through field hunting and content within the Arcane River and Grandis regions.
newFacts.whyItMatters: lib/classes.ts has a nodestoneSources field that data/classes.json never populates. This is a first-party fill for it.

newFacts.fact: The official guide's class roster includes Ren (Anima) with the link skill Grounded Body, and lists Erel Light and Sia Astelle as playable jobs on the 5th Job page - but gives Erel Light no link skill entry at all.
newFacts.whyItMatters: data/classes.json carries ren but data/class-guides/ has no ren.json (54 files, no Ren). Conversely the repo confidently ships Erel Light's link skill and NEXON does not document one.

heroicDistinctions.finding: None. Across all three pages there are ZERO occurrences of 'Reboot', 'Heroic', or 'Interactive'.

heroicDistinctions.interpretation: Link skills, 5th Job skills and the V Matrix are presented as world-type-agnostic. The Heroic-relevant clauses are the ones about TRADING and the MARKET, and none of these three systems involves either - nodestones drop from hunting and events, node enhancement consumes your own nodes, and links transfer only within your own account on one world. So for these three subsystems specifically, Interactive-world advice is NOT silently wrong for this owner.
heroicDistinctions.caveat: The one economic number on these pages, the 1,000,000 meso V Matrix slot reset, is trivially affordable in Heroic at 764% meso obtained. If anything the reset is cheaper in real terms for this owner than for an Interactive player.

guidanceForNextAgent.strongest: The link skill table is complete and first-party. Treat data/sources/nexon/skills.json linkSkillTable as outranking every wiki row for GMS link skill names, per-level values and unlock levels.
guidanceForNextAgent.mostUrgent: Seven numeric contradictions in data/classes.json - Invincible Belief cooldown, Empirical Knowledge per-stack, Thief's Cunning max, Mihile Knight's Watch, Mercedes return cooldown, Zero Rhinne's Blessing max, Ren Grounded Body, Illium link duration, Angelic Buster cooldown, Kain stack trigger, Lynn boss damage. Also one in lib/legion.ts: the Cygnus ATT vs ATT-and-Magic-ATT split is fictional.
guidanceForNextAgent.mostDelicate: Sia Astelle / Erel Light. The repo says Guiding Stars, Master Level 6, shared. NEXON says Tree of Stars, 3 levels, Sia Astelle only, no Erel Light entry. The Lv. 3 values agree exactly (+10% buff duration / +3% critical damage), which is strong evidence they are the same skill under two names rather than two different skills. The owner supplied an in-game tooltip saying Master Level 6 and shared, and an in-game tooltip outranks a guide page that may simply predate the Erel Light release. Do NOT overwrite the repo with 'Tree of Stars' on the strength of this page alone. Record both and ask the owner for a screenshot of the skill name.
guidanceForNextAgent.doNotTrust: Every V Matrix number on page 5904 describes the pre-v.269 system by NEXON's own admission. The 25/30 skill node and 50/55 boost node caps, and the Matrix Point mechanics, should be re-verified against a post-v.269 source before the app states them.
